title: Myeloproliferative neoplasms — PV, ET, PMF
subtitle: Philadelphia-negative MPNs driven by constitutive JAK-STAT signaling (JAK2 V617F, CALR, MPL) · goals: prevent thrombosis in PV/ET, control spleen, symptoms and anemia in MF, and transplant the fit high-risk MF patient
source: No Stanford Oncology Handbook chapter — compiled from WHO 2022 / ICC 2022 criteria · NCCN MPN · ELN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed; approvals against FDA labels, October 2026.

blocks.heading: Driver mutations
blocks.footnote: JAK2-negative erythrocytosis is not PV until exon 12 is excluded — go back to the secondary differential. CALR never occurs in PV (mutant CALR signals only through MPL). In ET, CALR = higher platelets but lower thrombosis risk than JAK2; in PMF, CALR type 1 is favorable and triple-negative is worst.

blocks.heading: Diagnosis (WHO 2022 · ICC 2022)
rows: Hb >16.5 (M) / >16.0 (F) or Hct >49% / >48% + trilineage marrow hypercellularity with pleomorphic mature megakaryocytes + JAK2 V617F or exon 12. Minor: subnormal EPO. All 3 major, or first 2 + minor. Marrow can be skipped if Hb >18.5 / >16.5 (Hct >55.5 / >49.5%) with JAK2 + low EPO — but it misses early fibrosis

Platelets ≥450 + marrow with large, hyperlobulated (“staghorn”) megakaryocytes, no left shift, reticulin ≤grade 1 + not another myeloid neoplasm + JAK2 / CALR / MPL. Minor: other clonal marker or no reactive cause. Marrow is required

Megakaryocyte proliferation with atypia (clustering, cloud-like nuclei), reticulin ≤grade 1, hypercellular, granulocytic ↑ / erythroid ↓ + driver or clonal marker + ≥1 minor: anemia, WBC ≥11, palpable spleen, ↑LDH
Same megakaryocyte atypia + reticulin/collagen grade 2–3 + clonal marker + ≥1 minor (above, or leukoerythroblastosis)

Prior PV/ET + grade 2–3 fibrosis + ≥2 of: anemia (post-PV: or loss of phlebotomy/cytoreduction need; post-ET: Hb ↓≥2 g/dL), leukoerythroblastosis, enlarging spleen (≥5 cm), constitutional symptoms, ↑LDH (post-ET) (IWG-MRT)
blocks.footnote: Prefibrotic PMF vs ET — same CBC, but prefibrotic PMF has worse survival and more fibrotic/leukemic progression. It turns on megakaryocyte morphology, so every suspected ET needs a marrow.

boxes: aspirin 81 mg daily; treat CV risk factors
observe, or aspirin 81 mg if JAK2+ or CV RFs
cytoreduce if symptoms or extreme platelets
or anagrelide; IFN if young / pregnancy
int-2 / high risk, fit: refer for allo-HCT

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Peripheral blood JAK2 V617F (qPCR, report VAF) → if negative: CALR + MPL (thrombocytosis / fibrosis) or JAK2 exon 12 (erythrocytosis). Most labs now run an MPN NGS panel up front
NGS for high-molecular-risk mutations: ASXL1, SRSF2, U2AF1 Q157, EZH2, IDH1/2 (+ TP53, RAS) — drive MIPSS70+ and transplant referral
BCR::ABL1 (PCR or FISH) in every thrombocytosis / leukocytosis — CML can present as isolated thrombocytosis
Erythrocytosis: serum EPO (low → PV; normal/high → secondary), ferritin/iron (iron deficiency masks PV), SpO2, sleep study, smoking/CO-Hb, testosterone/SGLT2i, renal/hepatic mass imaging
Thrombocytosis: exclude iron deficiency, inflammation/infection, asplenia, malignancy, bleeding (CRP, ferritin)
Marrow aspirate + biopsy with reticulin stain + karyotype; abdominal US for spleen; LDH, uric acid
Platelets >1000–1500 or any bleeding: vWF:RCo (ristocetin cofactor) + vWF antigen — acquired vWD; ratio <0.7 or RCo <30% → hold aspirin, cytoreduce

blocks.heading: Risk stratification
rows: High = age ≥60 OR prior thrombosis; low = neither. Leukocytosis, CV risk factors and JAK2 VAF add risk but are not in the score
Very low: ≤60, no thrombosis, JAK2 WT · low: ≤60, no thrombosis, JAK2+ · intermediate: >60, no thrombosis, JAK2 WT · high: prior thrombosis, or >60 + JAK2+
DIPSS (age >65, Hb <10 [2 pts], WBC >25, blasts ≥1%, constitutional sx) + unfavorable karyotype, plt <100, transfusion need. Median OS: low 185 · int-1 78 · int-2 35 · high 16 mo

Very-high-risk karyotype 4, unfavorable karyotype 3, ≥2 HMR mutations 3 / 1 HMR 2, absent CALR type 1 2, constitutional sx 2, severe anemia 2 (moderate 1), blasts ≥2% 1 → very low / low / intermediate / high / very high
Hb <11 (2), blasts ≥3% (2), CALR-unmutated (2), plt <150 (1), constitutional sx (1), +0.15/yr of age. Median OS: low NR · int-1 9.3 · int-2 4.4 · high 2 yr
blocks.footnote: Use MYSEC-PM, not DIPSS/IPSS, for secondary MF. HMR = ASXL1, SRSF2, U2AF1 Q157, EZH2, IDH1/2; TP53 (multi-hit) predicts leukemic transformation.

blocks.heading: Follow-up and progression
items: Stable PV/ET: CBC every 3–6 mo, symptom score (MPN-SAF TSS), spleen exam, CV risk factors; reassess risk category with each new thrombosis or birthday past 60
Suspect post-PV/ET MF: falling Hb or loss of phlebotomy need, rising LDH, leukoerythroblastosis, growing spleen, new constitutional symptoms → repeat marrow + NGS, restage with MYSEC-PM
Suspect accelerated/blast phase: circulating blasts ≥10%, new refractory cytopenias → marrow, karyotype, NGS (TP53), HLA typing
JAK2/CALR VAF is worth tracking on interferon (molecular response); not needed on HU

blocks.heading: Other MPNs (brief)
items: MPN-U — MPN features that fit no category (often early PMF or splanchnic thrombosis presentations); manage by the dominant phenotype
CNL — sustained neutrophilia ≥25 (≥80% segs/bands), no dysplasia; CSF3R T618I (~60–80%); ruxolitinib responses; allo-HCT for fit
CEL — clonal eosinophilia ≥1.5 with marrow abnormality; first exclude PDGFRA/B, FGFR1, JAK2 rearrangements (imatinib-sensitive PDGFR)

blocks.heading: Polycythemia vera — evidence
rows: <45% for everyone (CYTO-PV, n=365): CV death or major thrombosis 2.7% vs 9.8% at 45–50% (HR 3.91)
81–100 mg daily for all without contraindication (ECLAP: fewer thromboses)
PROUD-PV / CONTINUATION-PV (ropeg vs HU, early PV): 12-mo non-inferiority not met (CHR + normal spleen 21% vs 28%), but CHR at 36 mo 71% vs 51% and deeper JAK2 VAF falls. Responses accrue slowly
Low-PV (randomized phase 2, age ≤60): ropeg 100 µg q2wk + phlebotomy kept Hct ≤45% in 84% vs 60%; stopped early for efficacy
Ruxolitinib — RESPONSE (phase 3): Hct control + spleen response 21% vs 1%; MAJIC-PV (phase 2): CR 43% vs 26%, event-free survival HR 0.58
Rusfertide (hepcidin mimetic, VERIFY phase 3, n=293): no phlebotomy wk 20–32 76.9% vs 32.9%; Hct <45% 62.6% vs 14.4%. FDA 28 Aug 2026 (Mimrylo). Erythrocytosis only — not cytoreductive
blocks.footnote: HU resistance (ELN): need for phlebotomy, plt >400 + WBC >10, or no spleen response after 3 mo at ≥2 g/day; cytopenia at lowest effective dose; or intolerable toxicity (leg ulcers, mucositis).

blocks.heading: Essential thrombocythemia — evidence
rows: JAK2+ or CV risk factors: aspirin 81 mg. Low-risk CALR+: aspirin did not cut thrombosis but raised bleeding (retrospective) — observe. BID aspirin is an option if JAK2+ with CV risk factors (faster platelet turnover)
PT-1 (n=809, high risk, + aspirin): anagrelide arm more arterial thrombosis, serious bleeding and myelofibrosis, fewer VTE (composite OR 1.57) → HU first line

Ropeginterferon — SURPASS-ET (phase 3, HU-resistant/intolerant + WBC >10): durable ELN response 43% vs 6% vs anagrelide; thromboembolic events 1 vs 10 (FDA label). FDA 31 Aug 2026 (all adult ET). 96% Asian cohort
Cytoreduce to symptom control and plt <400–450; no evidence that normalizing counts alone prevents thrombosis in low-risk disease

blocks.heading: Myelofibrosis — JAK inhibitor choice
rows: Default first line, plt ≥50. COMFORT-I: SVR35 41.9% vs 0.7%, TSS50 46% vs 5%, deaths HR 0.50; COMFORT-II vs BAT: SVR35 28% vs 0%. Worsens anemia/plt early
JAKARTA (1L): SVR35 36% vs 1%. FREEDOM2 (post-rux): 36% vs 6% vs BAT. Thiamine (Wernicke in 4 at 500 mg)
Plt <50 (accelerated 2022). PERSIST-2 (plt ≤100): 200 mg BID SVR35 22% vs 3%, TSS50 32% vs 14%. Confirmatory PACIFICA (plt <50) not yet reported
Anemia (Hb <10), FDA 2023. MOMENTUM (JAKi-exposed, anemic): TSS50 25% vs 9% vs danazol + better transfusion independence. SIMPLIFY-1: SVR35 non-inferior to rux (26.5 vs 29%); symptoms not
blocks.footnote: Add-on combinations: spleen up, symptoms not, none approved. With ruxolitinib in JAKi-naive MF, SVR35 roughly doubled with pelabresib (MANIFEST-2: 66% vs 35%), navitoclax (TRANSFORM-1: 63% vs 32%), selinexor (SENTRY: 50% vs 28%) — symptom endpoints not met in all three; pelabresib has an excess leukemic transformation signal; US filing deferred.

blocks.heading: Anemia, transplant, blast phase
items: Anemia of MF: ESA if EPO <500 and not transfusion-dependent; danazol (monitor LFTs, PSA); switch to momelotinib. Luspatercept (INDEPENDENCE, transfusion-dependent on JAKi): RBC-TI 23% vs 13%, primary endpoint not met (P=0.067) — off-label

Allo-HCT — only curative therapy. Refer DIPSS int-2/high, MIPSS70+ high, HMR mutations, transfusion dependence, plt <100, TP53/complex karyotype, age generally <70. Continue JAKi up to conditioning (taper over days)
MTSS (post-transplant): age ≥57, KPS <90, plt <150, WBC >25, HLA-mismatched unrelated donor, ASXL1, non-CALR/MPL driver → 5-yr OS 83 / 64 / 37 / 22%

Accelerated (10–19% blasts) / blast phase (≥20%): median OS ~3–6 mo. HMA + venetoclax gives CR/CRi ~40–45% but median OS only ~7–8 mo (retrospective series) — use as a bridge to allo-HCT, the only route to long-term survival. Intensive induction gives no OS edge without transplant; IDH-mutant: ivosidenib/enasidenib

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — dosing, toxicity and monitoring, special situations, key trials

blocks.heading: Agents — dosing
rows: 81 mg daily; 81 mg BID option in JAK2+ ET with CV risk factors. Hold if vWF:RCo <30%
250–500 mL to Hct <45%; check CBC q4–6 wk once stable. No iron
500 mg BID (15–20 mg/kg/day) → titrate to counts; avoid in pregnancy
PV: 100 µg SC q2wk (50 if on HU) → +50 µg q2wk to max 500 µg until counts stable. ET: 250 → 350 (wk 2) → 500 µg q2wk from wk 4
19 mg SC weekly → titrate (9.5–108 mg) to hold Hct <45%; CBC q2–4 wk during titration
Label: 0.5 mg QID or 1 mg BID (0.5 mg BID often used) → ↑ ≤0.5 mg/day per week; max 10 mg/day, 2.5 mg/dose. ECG + cardiac history (QT, palpitations, HF)
By platelets: >200 → 20 mg BID · 100–200 → 15 BID · 50–<100 → 5 BID; titrate. PV: 10 mg BID
400 mg daily (plt ≥50); 200 mg if CrCl 15–29 or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Thiamine level at baseline; replete before start; prophylactic antiemetic
200 mg BID (plt <50); avoid with QTc >480, active bleeding
200 mg daily; no platelet floor on the label (MOMENTUM enrolled plt ≥25); dose-reduce for cytopenias per label
200 mg TID (600 mg/day); LFTs, PSA in men
Epoetin alfa 40,000 U weekly or darbepoetin 150–300 µg q2wk if EPO <500; stop if no response by 12 wk

blocks.heading: Response definitions
rows: Hct <45% without phlebotomy, plt ≤400, WBC ≤10, normal spleen, no disease symptoms
Plt ≤400, WBC <10, normal spleen, no symptoms, no thrombosis/bleeding
SVR35 = ≥35% spleen volume reduction on MRI/CT at wk 24 · TSS50 = ≥50% fall in MFSAF total symptom score · anemia: transfusion independence ≥12 wk

blocks.heading: Toxicity and monitoring
items: Hydroxyurea: macrocytosis (expected), cytopenias, leg / oral ulcers, NMSC (annual skin exam). Leukemogenic risk is low and not proven

Interferons: boxed warning — depression/suicidality, autoimmune thyroiditis, retinopathy, hepatotoxicity. Baseline + periodic TSH, LFTs, eye exam, mood screen; avoid with uncontrolled psychiatric or autoimmune disease

JAK inhibitors: anemia/thrombocytopenia (nadir wk 8–12), herpes zoster (recombinant zoster vaccine), HBV reactivation (screen HBsAg/anti-HBc), TB, PML, NMSC, lipids ↑. MACE/VTE/malignancy class warnings from tofacitinib in RA
Ruxolitinib discontinuation syndrome: abrupt stop → symptom/spleen rebound, rarely SIRS-like collapse — taper, steroids if needed
Fedratinib: Wernicke encephalopathy — thiamine monthly early, stop for confusion/ataxia/vision change and give IV thiamine; GI toxicity, amylase/lipase
Rusfertide: injection-site reactions (56%), anemia (16%) per label; may worsen thrombocytosis — monitor platelets, may need cytoreduction; induced iron restriction is intended — don't give iron

blocks.heading: Special situations
items: Splanchnic vein thrombosis / Budd-Chiari: test JAK2 V617F (then CALR) even with normal counts — portal hypertension masks erythrocytosis and thrombocytosis. Long-term anticoagulation + cytoreduction (IFN or HU)
Pregnancy: aspirin throughout; peg-IFN if cytoreduction needed (stop HU, anagrelide, JAKi before conception); Hct <45% in PV; LMWH for 6 wk postpartum, antepartum too if prior thrombosis
Surgery: control counts first (Hct <45%, plt near normal); hold aspirin 7 days for high-bleed procedures; aggressive VTE prophylaxis — perioperative thrombosis and bleeding both rise
Extreme thrombocytosis (>1000–1500): acquired vWD → bleeding, not clotting; check vWF:RCo, hold aspirin if low, cytoreduce. Plateletpheresis only for acute thrombosis/bleeding
Pruritus (aquagenic, PV): antihistamines, SSRIs (paroxetine), narrowband UVB; IFN or ruxolitinib for refractory itch
Thrombosis on therapy: arterial → aspirin + cytoreduce; venous → DOAC/warfarin long term + cytoreduce; reassess Hct/plt control

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Ropeg vs HU: 12-mo NI missed; CHR 36 mo 71% vs 51%
Ropeg + phlebotomy in low-risk PV: response 84% vs 60%
Rux vs BAT, HU-R/I PV: composite 21% vs 1%
Rux vs BAT: CR 43% vs 26%; EFS HR 0.58
Rusfertide vs placebo: no phlebotomy 77% vs 33%
HU vs anagrelide in high-risk ET: HU superior (OR 1.57)
Ropeg vs anagrelide, 2L ET: response 43% vs 6%
Momelotinib vs danazol, anemic: TSS50 25% vs 9%
Momelotinib vs rux: SVR35 non-inferior; TSS not
